correctness.rationale: The equation determines a unique formal solution by induction in x: the x^n coefficient on the right only sees a_0 through a_{n-1}. The published Thm. 7.1 applies to this exact equation and gives the nonnegative monomial coefficients, degree n² and leading coefficient 1/n. For q≥1, retaining the leading monomial gives the lower bound, and replacing each monomial q^j by q^{n²} gives a_n(q)≤q^{n²}a_n(1). The q=1 quadratic's discriminant 1−6x+x² has its nearest zero at 3−2√2>1/6; the branch with constant term 1 takes value 2 at 1/6, giving a_n(1)≤2·6^n. For each q≥2, the resulting bounds prove the logarithmic limit and, by Cauchy–Hadamard, zero radius. Algebraic branches in characteristic zero converge locally; P-recursive sequences need not converge as ordinary series but have coefficient magnitude bounded by exp(O(n log n)), by dividing by the eventual nonzero highest-shift coefficient and iterating a polynomial bound on the maximum of a moving window. The q^{n²}/n lower bound contradicts that ceiling. The q=0 and q=1 quadratic branches are analytic at zero and algebraic. The bounds in fact give a uniform error in log(a_n(q))/n²−log q for q≥2; it suffices to state the fixed-q result. The frozen check.py was inspected, not executed; its low-order calculations do not prove the infinite assertions.

value.rationale: Analyticity and holonomicity are natural invariants, and this is a useful explanatory corollary. As an independent finding, however, it gives only the coefficient comparison already immediate from the prior positivity/degree theorem and the standard consequences of superfactorial growth. It supplies neither a new informative scale within the q≥2 regime nor an asymptotic equivalent or additional nonmechanical invariant. An improved asymptotic would be a different claim, not a repair of this frozen classification.
